question: Does field-star translation correction improve agreement with catalogue-predicted displacement on additional stars in the saved fields?
selection: Default exposures-cadence selection from each shipped motion_analysis.json. Candidate Gaia stars have 11 <= G <= 16.5, finite proper motion, no catalogue variable flag, lie at least 12 native pixels inside the first image, and at least 10 pixels from the featured target. Sort by SHA-256 of source_id; take the first 40 per field before measuring. Retain every refusal and all fields.
method: Unmodified production analyseMotion on native pixels, leaving each target out of its own reference ensemble. No threshold or engine changes in response to this benchmark.
baseline: The same accepted target centroids and visit grouping without reference-star translation correction. Both use identical exposures, catalogue truth and the calibrated method's displacement uncertainty for the discrepancy diagnostic.
truth: Gaia catalogue positions propagated with proper motion and precise positive parallax where available to the two endpoint visit dates. Compare east/north displacement vectors, not their scalar magnitudes alone.
metrics: median vector residual in arcseconds for each method on the identical accepted sample
residual above 3 and 5 times the same displacement uncertainty
all per-field results and all refused cases
limitations: A deterministic retrospective benchmark of an already developed engine on saved example fields; not a blind prospective test.
Catalogue agreement is not source discovery completeness, a sky-wide false-positive rate, or independent scientific replication.
Stars share images and reference ensembles. They are correlated and cannot be counted as independent trials.
Gaia predictions are not exact ground truth: catalogue parameter covariance, unresolved binaries and radial velocity are not modeled here.
The comparator isolates translation correction on accepted centroids; it does not compare whole products or all their quality rules.
Discrepancy screens use the production error scale; they are diagnostics, not calibrated tail probabilities.
